hypothesis_change_reason: Dispatch 131 localized the blocker to core_digest() deriving the core's identity from a live working tree, and routed it to the Agent Core repository as a core code defect. This dispatch tested that premise directly against the guard's own public interface and falsified it. The pin mechanism already exists and is core-authored; the defect is that no controller caller ever sets it.

narrative.FINDING: The orchestration red is NOT caused by core_digest() being structurally unable to pin an identity. AC_CORE_ROOT is already a first-class, core-authored pin knob in the canonical validators, and executing the shipped validator with it set makes the postrun verdict deterministic and finite. The actual defect is one level up and much smaller: no controller or postrun caller ever sets AC_CORE_ROOT, so validate-ac-project.py:116 silently falls through to its default of the LIVE core directory.
narrative.OBSERVED_FAILURE: python .opencode/scripts/validate-ac-project.py -> FAIL, 'materialization stale: canonical-core-revision-changed' + 30 managed-file-content-mismatch. With AC_CORE_ROOT pinned to a read-only git-archive extraction of a committed ref, the SAME shipped validator consumes the knob and returns a finite named delta: 91 mismatches @v1.0.0, 92 @origin/main, 99 @origin/fix/shared-silent-process-contract, versus 30 against the live tree.
narrative.HYPOTHESIS: If dispatch 131's premise were right, pinning the guard to a committed ref could not change the shape of the verdict, and no supported mechanism could make the postrun check reproducible without a change to the core. Measured: (a) two back-to-back guard runs against the live core produced BYTE-IDENTICAL JSON, so core_digest() is deterministic over whatever directory it is handed; (b) the canonical validators already read AC_CORE_ROOT and validate-managed-runtime.py even self-tests that the knob propagates into the validator subprocess and that a misleading project core cannot steal authority; (c) the knob demonstrably works when set. The live-tree dependence is therefore a caller-default defect, not a hashing-function defect.
narrative.CHANGE: Measurement only. No repository file, no core file, no manifest, no lock, no lifecycle file, no env var persisted. The core was read with `git archive` only, and every extraction was written into this project's .tmp. The AC_CORE_ROOT assignments existed only inside single PowerShell tool invocations and were not exported to the controller environment.
narrative.RESULT: Hypothesis confirmed and the prior hypothesis falsified. The blocker is re-localized from 'unaddressable core identity-function defect' to a named, controller-owned invocation omission at .opencode/scripts/validate-ac-project.py:115-117, with a one-line remedy (pin AC_CORE_ROOT to a committed core ref in the POSTRUN chain). Owner routing therefore changes from the Agent Core repository to THIS repository's controller. W57 cannot apply it: the postrun chain is not a Wave worker's surface and W57's own report forbids a worker from materializing. A second, separable prerequisite remains and is also not W57's: the project matches NO attested ref, so a zero-delta pin target requires the core to commit and tag its current canonical bytes.

prior_hypothesis_falsified.prior_claim: core_digest() hashes the core's live working tree, so the pinned identity is not addressable, is not reproducible by any commit, and moves every time the core edits its canonical sources. Therefore re-materialization cannot converge to any fixed point.
prior_hypothesis_falsified.falsifying_measurement_1_determinism: materialization_guard.py --check --core D:\Projeler\.agents-core run twice back-to-back produced byte-identical output (30 mismatches, canonical-core-revision-changed present, run1 == run2 True). The function is a deterministic function of the tree it is given. Dispatch 131's 18 -> 30 growth, which it offered as non-convergence observed directly, is the core's own WIP moving during that dispatch, not non-determinism in the guard.
prior_hypothesis_falsified.falsifying_measurement_2_the_knob_exists: .opencode/scripts/validate-ac-project.py:115-117 reads os.environ['AC_CORE_ROOT'] and falls back to (repo.parent / '.agents-core'). .opencode/scripts/validate-managed-runtime.py:39-50 reads the same variable and raises a named error instructing the caller to set it. validate-managed-runtime.py:3707-3742 self-tests that the variable propagates into the validator subprocess and errors with 'AC_CORE_ROOT lost authority to misleading project core'. The pin mechanism is core-authored, core-documented and core-tested; it is not missing.
prior_hypothesis_falsified.falsifying_measurement_3_the_knob_works: Running the SHIPPED validate-ac-project.py with AC_CORE_ROOT pointed at a read-only git-archive extraction of each committed ref returned a finite, named, reproducible delta: 91 @v1.0.0(73c1b7d), 92 @origin/main(0a8a832), 99 @origin/fix/shared-silent-process-contract(65d8a46), 30 @LIVE. A verdict that is a deterministic function of a pinned ref is exactly what 131 said could not exist.
prior_hypothesis_falsified.conclusion: The 'unpinnable core identity' root cause is refuted. The correct root cause is an unset environment variable in the caller's fallback branch.

the_actual_defect.code:
raw_core = os.environ.get("AC_CORE_ROOT")
core_candidate = Path(raw_core).resolve() if raw_core else (repo.parent / ".agents-core").resolve()
core = core_candidate if (core_candidate / "AC_MANIFEST.json").is_file() else None
the_actual_defect.why: The guard takes a DIRECTORY, never a revision, and the validator's default binds it to the live core directory. D:\Projeler\.agents-core is concurrently running its own program with uncommitted WIP, so the postrun verdict is a function of a moving target.
the_actual_defect.caller_audit: grep for AC_CORE_ROOT across .opencode/scripts/run-wave-program.py, wave_state_engine.py, validate-managed-runtime.py, validate-agent-parity.py, validate-wave-orchestration.py, validate-wave-authoring.py and materialization_guard.py returns ONLY the validators' own readers and validate-managed-runtime.py's self-test. No controller or postrun caller ever SETS the variable. The fallback branch is therefore the branch that always executes.
the_actual_defect.remedy: In the controller-owned POSTRUN chain, set AC_CORE_ROOT to a read-only extraction of a committed core ref before invoking the postrun validators. This changes no core file, requires no materialization, and makes the verdict reproducible.

second_separable_prerequisite.statement: The project matches NO attested core ref, so pinning alone yields a reproducible RED, not green. The smallest delta is against the LIVE tree (30), not against any ref (91/92/99), which shows the project was materialized from core bytes that are NEWER than every committed ref.
second_separable_prerequisite.implication: A zero-delta pin target requires the core to commit and tag its current canonical bytes. The core's WIP is uncommitted and the core is running its own program, so this is also not W57's to perform.
second_separable_prerequisite.owner: Agent Core repository D:\Projeler\.agents-core (commit/tag) and this repository's controller (pin invocation).
second_separable_prerequisite.honest_limit: This dispatch does NOT claim that pinning turns the postrun check green. It claims only that pinning turns an unbounded, moving verdict into a bounded, named, reproducible one - which is what makes the remaining delta actionable at all.
